domain_label: Code-Gen Models & Execution Feedback (LLM Engineering subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope is code LLM selection, fine-tuning, execution-feedback loops, repo/API grounding, stack specialization, and orchestration
evaluation is execution-based (pass@k) unless project overrides
a working code LLM inference endpoint is assumed; hardware procurement is out of scope
exclusions: code review UI/UX and developer tooling beyond generation pipeline
hardware procurement and data center management
code model serving infrastructure below application API layer

competency_questions.question: What execution-based benchmark is used to measure code generation capability and how is pass@k computed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CODEX_BENCH and PASS_K define benchmark and estimator

competency_questions.question: How is pass@k computed without bias and what sample count is required?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PASS_K defines unbiased estimator with n>=k requirement

competency_questions.question: How is the base code LLM selected balancing benchmark performance, license, and hardware fit?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CODELLM_SELECT covers license, benchmark, and VRAM criteria

competency_questions.question: How is the selected model fine-tuned for domain specialization and how is catastrophic forgetting controlled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CODEGEN_FINETUNE covers SFT and forgetting mitigation

competency_questions.question: How does the test-driven generation loop work and what stopping criteria prevent runaway repair?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TDG_LOOP defines loop, error injection, iteration cap, token budget

competency_questions.question: How is the execution sandbox secured and what resource limits are enforced?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EXEC_SANDBOX covers isolation, network, CPU/memory limits

competency_questions.question: How is repository and API context retrieved and injected to enable library-aware generation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REPO_CONTEXT and API_GROUND cover retrieval and injection

competency_questions.question: How are stack-specific prompts designed and kept current with framework evolution?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STACK_SPEC covers versioning and staleness detection

competency_questions.question: How does web/HTML and Python data-science code generation differ in specialization requirements?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WEB_HTML_GEN and PY_DATA_GEN cover distinct requirements

competency_questions.question: How is functional correctness evaluated beyond pass@k (mutation testing, property-based tests)?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FUNC_CORRECT covers mutation and property-based testing

competency_questions.question: How is security of generated code enforced to prevent injection and credential leakage?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SECURITY_SCAN covers SAST, injection, secret scanning

competency_questions.question: How are benchmark Goodhart effects detected and mitigated to prevent capability overestimation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOODHART_BENCH covers contamination and held-out eval

competency_questions.question: When does specialist outperform generalist and how is the tradeoff decided?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SPEC_VS_GEN covers cost-benefit and distribution scope

competency_questions.question: How is reinforcement learning from execution feedback implemented and how is reward hacking prevented?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RLEF covers RL objective, KL penalty, and reward hacking audit

glossary.definition: fraction of problems where at least one of k generated samples passes all unit tests; estimated unbiasedly with n>=k samples
benchmark of 164 Python programming problems with unit tests introduced by Chen et al. 2021 (Codex paper)
isolated container/VM environment for safely running model-generated code during evaluation and feedback loops
iterative loop generating code, executing in sandbox, injecting pass/fail and error messages back to model for repair
reinforcement learning from execution feedback; using test pass/fail outcomes as RL reward signal to align model toward functional correctness
phenomenon where code model optimizes benchmark pass@k through contamination or narrow overfitting without improving real-world coding capability
relevant code snippets, imports, type stubs, and related functions retrieved from the target repository and injected into the code generation prompt
adaptation of code generation prompts, examples, and evaluation criteria to a specific programming language or framework stack
evaluation technique that inserts small syntactic mutations into code and checks whether tests detect the mutant, measuring test suite quality

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for code-generation work units in absence of supplied datasets; informed by Chen et al. 2021 (Codex/HumanEval), Hunt & Thomas (Pragmatic Programmer), and practitioner domain knowledge
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Chen et al. 2021 arxiv:2107.03374; Hunt & Thomas The Pragmatic Programmer (2nd ed.)
grounding_limits: domain-general heuristic priors for code LLM engineering

nodes.definition: Establish pass@k evaluation on HumanEval (164 Python problems) and related execution-based benchmarks as the standard for measuring code-generation model capability.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new execution-grounded benchmark replaces HumanEval as standard

cons.claim: pass@k gives execution-grounded correctness signal avoiding proxy metrics
cons.example: pass@1 at T=0.2 and pass@100 at T=0.8 disentangle greedy vs diversity

failure_modes: HumanEval contamination inflates scores for models trained after 2021
post-training data scraping including HumanEval solutions
acceptance_tests: benchmark contamination
gaming pass@k with high-temp sampling
ignoring distribution beyond Python algorithms
revisit_triggers: pass@1 and pass@100 reported separately
results reproducible with fixed seed

nodes.definition: Compute unbiased pass@k via the Chen et al. estimator using n>=k generated samples per problem, avoiding naive averaging that overestimates.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new debiasing estimator published or k target shifts

cons.claim: Unbiased estimator prevents over-estimation from small sample pass rates
cons.example: n=20,k=1 gives same expectation as n=1 sample average

failure_modes: Requires generating n>>k samples; expensive at large n
n=200 for pass@100 multiplies inference cost 200x
acceptance_tests: undercounting with n=k only
mixing temperatures across problems
revisit_triggers: estimator matches analytic formula for a held fixture
confidence intervals provided
handoff_artifact_required: compute budget changes forcing smaller n

nodes.definition: Select a pre-trained code LLM (StarCoder2, DeepSeek-Coder, CodeLlama, etc.) appropriate for the target stack and license constraints, weighing benchmark performance against ToS/license.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new SOTA code LLM released or license terms change

cons.claim: Matching model to target stack avoids costly fine-tuning to fill capability gaps
cons.example: DeepSeek-Coder-33B outperforms CodeLlama-34B on Python/SQL by ~8pp pass@1

failure_modes: Goodhart pressure: top-benchmark model may be contaminated or not transfer to prod tasks
leaderboard-optimized models fail on internal codebase idioms
acceptance_tests: license incompatibility discovered post-selection
benchmark contamination
VRAM/cost mismatch at inference
revisit_triggers: license reviewed and signed off before selection finalized
hardware fit verified with profiled VRAM usage
benchmark scores sourced from uncontaminated held-out eval
handoff_artifact_required: target stack expands to new language

nodes.definition: Design and operate a secure, isolated execution environment (container/sandbox) for running model-generated code during test-driven generation feedback loops.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: container escape CVE published or latency SLA changes

cons.claim: Prevents arbitrary code execution from escaping to host; enables safe automated eval
cons.example: gVisor/nsjail contain even os.system() calls in generated code

failure_modes: Sandbox overhead adds latency per generation; container spin-up 50-200ms per attempt
100 samples x 200ms = 20s latency in tight feedback loops
acceptance_tests: container escape via unpatched kernel vulnerability
resource exhaustion DOS
false-pass due to incorrect test oracle
revisit_triggers: sandbox must block network access by default
resource limits enforced: 10s CPU, 256MB RAM per execution
all syscalls outside allowlist rejected

nodes.definition: Implement the iterative loop that generates candidate code, executes it in sandbox, collects pass/fail + stderr signals, and re-prompts the model with failure context for repair.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new repair strategy (e.g., tree-search) replaces single repair chain

cons.claim: Execution feedback reduces error rate dramatically vs single-shot; 3-5 iterations typical
cons.example: AlphaCode uses sampling+filtering; Self-Debug uses trace injection for repair

failure_modes: Repair loops compound token cost; runaway loops on adversarial inputs
GPT-4 repair loop: 5 iterations x 2K tokens = 10K tokens per problem
acceptance_tests: infinite repair loop on unsolvable problems
error message leaking solution hints into prompt
silent wrong answer (passes tests, incorrect logic)
revisit_triggers: max_iterations capped (e.g., 5)
token budget hard stop
distinct test oracle from problem description
handoff_artifact_required: cost per token drops enabling more iterations

nodes.definition: Retrieve and inject relevant repository context (imports, type stubs, related functions, docstrings) into the code generation prompt to enable library-aware and repo-aware generation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: context window length changes or new retrieval strategy available

cons.claim: Repository context closes import/type-error gap; enables completion of real-world tasks
cons.example: RepoFusion/RepoCoder show +15pp on CrossCodeEval vs file-level baselines

failure_modes: Context retrieval latency and token cost compound; irrelevant context hurts generation
BM25 retrieval fetches wrong files for ambiguous function names
acceptance_tests: token overflow from over-fetching context
stale cache serving outdated code
circular import context causing confusion
revisit_triggers: retrieved context fits within context window with 20% headroom
retrieval precision verified on held-out repo tasks
import resolution tested on multi-file scenarios
handoff_artifact_required: repo size grows beyond indexing budget

nodes.definition: Design and maintain stack-specific system prompts, few-shot examples, and output format constraints for each target language/framework (Python, TypeScript/React, HTML/CSS, SQL).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: framework major version release or new target stack added

cons.claim: Stack-specific prompts cut syntax/idiom errors by encoding conventions explicitly
cons.example: React hooks prompt reduces useState misuse; SQL prompt enforces parameterized queries

failure_modes: Prompt proliferation creates maintenance burden; stale prompts mislead model
deprecated API in few-shot examples causes model to generate removed syntax
acceptance_tests: outdated idiom examples teaching deprecated patterns
prompt conflicts between stack and general instructions
format constraint too rigid for edge-case outputs
revisit_triggers: each stack prompt versioned and reviewed per framework major release
few-shot examples tested for correctness in sandbox
format constraints machine-parseable
handoff_artifact_required: model version change alters prompt sensitivity

nodes.definition: Ground code generation in accurate API signatures, deprecation status, and usage patterns by injecting retrieved API documentation or tool-call schemas into context.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: library major version release or API deprecation batch

cons.claim: Injecting current API docs prevents hallucinated method names and deprecated signatures
cons.example: pandas 2.0: model without grounding still generates df.append() (removed)

failure_modes: Doc retrieval latency and token cost; incorrect retrieval worsens output
wrong version of numpy docs causes dtype mismatch errors
acceptance_tests: version mismatch between injected docs and runtime
hallucinated parameters not caught by doc retrieval
doc corpus outdated
revisit_triggers: API signatures validated against installed package version
deprecated APIs filtered from retrieval corpus
grounding reduces hallucinated attribute errors by measurable margin
handoff_artifact_required: new API added to target library

nodes.definition: Fine-tune the selected code base model on domain/task-specific code data (e.g., internal codebase, stack-specific examples) using SFT to close the gap vs generic pretraining.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: domain code distribution shifts or base model updated

cons.claim: Domain SFT can close large performance gap on internal codebase idioms vs generic model
cons.example: 10K internal examples SFT yields +20pp pass@1 on internal tasks

failure_modes: Risk of catastrophic forgetting on general coding; data quality critical
SFT on low-quality internal code degrades HumanEval baseline by 5pp
acceptance_tests: catastrophic forgetting of base coding capability
data contamination from eval tasks
overfitting to narrow dataset idioms
revisit_triggers: HumanEval baseline preserved within 2pp after fine-tuning
eval on held-out internal tasks shows improvement
data deduplication applied before training

nodes.definition: Generate synthetic code training examples via model self-play, problem-solution generation, or execution-filtered synthesis to augment scarce labeled code data.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: eval benchmark updated or generation model changed

cons.claim: Execution-filtered synthetic data provides large-scale correctness-grounded training signal
cons.example: AlphaCode generates 1M solutions, filters by test pass to get high-quality set

failure_modes: Mode collapse: synthetic data amplifies base model blind spots
if base model systematically misuses asyncio, synthetic data propagates error
acceptance_tests: deduplication failure causing train/test leakage
synthetic data not diverse enough
filter over-selects easy problems
revisit_triggers: synthetic data deduplicated against eval benchmarks
execution filter pass rate reported
diversity metrics (problem type distribution) tracked

nodes.definition: Detect and mitigate Goodhart effects where models optimize benchmark metrics without improving real-world code quality, via contamination checks, held-out eval, and functional diversity testing.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new benchmark released or training data pipeline changes

cons.claim: Prevents silent capability overestimation; forces honest capability reporting
cons.example: GPT-4 scores ~90% HumanEval but underperforms on novel algorithmic variants

failure_modes: Contamination detection heuristics have false positive/negative rates
n-gram overlap misses semantic paraphrase contamination
acceptance_tests: semantic paraphrase contamination undetected by n-gram overlap
internal eval too correlated with public benchmark
held-out tasks not representative of prod distribution
revisit_triggers: contamination scan run before any benchmark reported
at least one held-out internal suite reported alongside public benchmark
diversity metrics tracked across problem types

nodes.definition: Evaluate whether a fine-tuned specialist code model outperforms a larger generalist enough on the narrow target task to justify the fine-tuning and serving overhead.
inputs: benchmark results for specialist and generalist

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new generalist SOTA released or target task scope changes

cons.claim: Specialist can match or exceed much larger generalist on narrow tasks at fraction of inference cost
cons.example: 7B domain specialist matches 70B generalist on target stack at 10x less cost

failure_modes: Specialist advantage erodes quickly outside its training distribution; orchestration adds latency
specialist fails on adjacent tasks requiring generalist fallback
acceptance_tests: narrow task definition that overfits specialist benefit
ignoring orchestration overhead in cost model
serving specialist + generalist compounding infrastructure cost
revisit_triggers: comparison run on identical hardware
held-out task set covers distribution tail
cost model includes serving overhead not just inference per query
handoff_artifact_required: new generalist model release shifts cost-performance frontier

nodes.definition: Profile and optimize code generation inference latency and cost per token across sampling budget, context length, and serving configuration to meet product SLAs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: hardware changes or SLA targets renegotiated

cons.claim: Latency/cost profiling prevents product-blocking surprises at deployment
cons.example: 8-bit quantization cuts serving cost 40% with <1pp pass@1 regression

failure_modes: Quantization/batching tradeoffs vary non-linearly with sequence length and load
aggressive quantization degrades long-context repo generation more than short snippets
acceptance_tests: quantization-induced accuracy regression underestimated
KV cache sizing causing OOM under burst load
latency SLA negotiated without profiling data
revisit_triggers: latency p99 measured under target load profile
cost per generation tracked and compared to budget
quantization accuracy delta verified on target eval

nodes.definition: Evaluate generated code for functional correctness beyond benchmark pass@k: property-based testing, mutation testing, and fuzzing to stress-test correctness claims.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new correctness evaluation framework available

cons.claim: Mutation testing reveals superficially-passing code with logical gaps that unit tests miss
cons.example: code passing 5 unit tests killed by 40% of mutations indicates fragile logic

failure_modes: Property-based and mutation testing expensive; requires domain property specifications
writing property specs for complex algorithms requires expert time
acceptance_tests: oracle gap: tests pass but logic wrong
mutation testing too slow for CI loop
property specs too weak to catch real bugs
revisit_triggers: mutation kill rate >60% required
at least 3 property-based tests per category
fuzz testing for all string/IO-handling functions

nodes.definition: Specialize code generation for HTML/CSS/JS/React front-end tasks including component generation, accessibility compliance, and responsive layout synthesis.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: component library major version or accessibility standard update

cons.claim: Front-end specialization with component library grounding dramatically reduces hallucinated props
cons.example: shadcn/ui doc injection reduces invalid prop errors by >50%

failure_modes: HTML/CSS generation difficult to unit-test automatically; visual correctness requires rendering
generated layout correct syntactically but visually broken on mobile
acceptance_tests: missing accessibility attributes (ARIA)
invalid HTML nesting
CSS specificity conflicts
visual breakage not caught by string comparison
revisit_triggers: HTML validates against W3C validator
accessibility audit passes WCAG 2.1 AA for generated components
component renders in headless browser test

nodes.definition: Specialize code generation for Python data-science tasks: pandas/numpy/sklearn idioms, vectorized operations, DataFrame shape correctness, and reproducibility (seed, split).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: pandas/numpy major version release or new vectorization patterns

cons.claim: Stack-aware prompts with DataFrame shape tests catch broadcasting errors at generation time
cons.example: shape assertion test catches (1000,1) vs (1000,) mismatch immediately

failure_modes: pandas API churn: grounding on wrong version causes silent deprecation errors
df.append() removed in pandas 2.0; model still generates it without versioned docs
acceptance_tests: vectorized vs loop confusion causing 100x slowdown
DataFrame shape mismatch silently producing wrong results
random seed omission causing irreproducibility
revisit_triggers: generated code passes DataFrame shape assertions
vectorization verified: no explicit Python loops on large arrays
random seeds set and documented
handoff_artifact_required: data schema changes in production pipeline

nodes.definition: Train code LLMs with RL-based objectives using execution outcomes (pass/fail, partial credit from test subsets) as reward signal to align generation toward functional correctness.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new RL algorithm or reward shaping strategy demonstrated

cons.claim: Execution reward directly optimizes functional correctness beyond SFT behavioral cloning
cons.example: CodeRL/PPOCoder show +5-10pp pass@1 over SFT baseline on HumanEval

failure_modes: Reward hacking: model learns to pass tests without generalizable logic; KL collapse risk
model exploits test oracle: generates try/except blocks that catch all exceptions
acceptance_tests: reward hacking via test oracle exploitation
KL collapse producing degenerate outputs
reward variance too high for stable RL training
revisit_triggers: reward hacking audit: inspect solutions that pass all tests but fail mutation
KL divergence tracked against base policy threshold
RL training reward curve shows consistent improvement without collapse

nodes.definition: Integrate static analysis and vulnerability scanning (SAST, secret detection, injection pattern checks) into the code generation pipeline to prevent insecure code from reaching production.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new OWASP vulnerability class or SAST tool update

cons.claim: SAST gate prevents SQL injection, XSS, hardcoded credentials from reaching code review
cons.example: Semgrep rule catches f-string SQL query generation immediately

failure_modes: High false-positive rate from SAST creates alert fatigue; SAST misses novel patterns
legacy SAST rules flag safe parameterized queries as injection risks
acceptance_tests: false negative on novel injection patterns
false positive alert fatigue causing rule disablement
SAST not integrated into generation loop (post-hoc only)
revisit_triggers: SAST runs on every generated code sample before returning to user
zero hardcoded credential false negatives tolerated
OWASP Top-10 patterns covered by rule set
handoff_artifact_required: new code pattern becomes common in generated output

nodes.definition: Generate diverse candidate solutions via temperature and nucleus sampling, then select the best via verifier scoring, majority vote, or test-weighted ranking.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new verifier strategy or compute budget changes

cons.claim: Best-of-n with execution filter dramatically improves pass@1 vs greedy without fine-tuning
cons.example: n=50 with test filter raises pass@1 from 40% to 65% on HumanEval

failure_modes: Cost scales linearly with n; high temperature increases diverse but incorrect solutions
n=100 at $0.01/1K tokens = $1 per problem at 1K tokens average
acceptance_tests: temperature too high producing incoherent candidates
verifier overfit to surface patterns not correctness
best-of-n masking latency from user
revisit_triggers: selection oracle tested independently of generator
diversity measured (distinct ASTs)
cost per query tracked against budget
handoff_artifact_required: sampling distribution changes with model update

nodes.definition: Ensure input docstrings and problem specifications provided to the code generator are complete, unambiguous, and include input/output examples to maximize generation accuracy.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: benchmark format changes or docstring standard updated

cons.claim: Structured docstrings with I/O examples reduce model ambiguity and improve pass@1 by 10-15pp
cons.example: adding 3 I/O examples to docstring raises ChatGPT pass@1 from 55% to 68% on MBPP

failure_modes: Over-specified docstrings may inadvertently provide solution hints leaking to benchmark
docstring includes loop structure hint that trivializes the algorithmic challenge
acceptance_tests: ambiguous docstring causing wrong function interpretation
missing edge cases in examples
type annotation mismatch between docstring and test oracle
revisit_triggers: docstring completeness checklist satisfied
at least 3 I/O examples provided
type annotations present and consistent with test oracle

nodes.definition: Integrate code generation specialists into multi-model orchestration pipelines: routing queries to appropriate specialists, aggregating outputs, and handling fallback to generalist models.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new specialist added or query distribution shifts

cons.claim: Routing code queries to specialists reduces cost vs always calling large generalist
cons.example: routing 80% queries to 7B specialist saves 60% vs always using 70B generalist

failure_modes: Routing errors send queries to wrong specialist; orchestration latency adds overhead
router misclassifies SQL query as Python, specialist returns hallucinated schema
acceptance_tests: routing classifier degrading silently on distribution shift
orchestration latency exceeding SLA
fallback loop compounding cost
revisit_triggers: router accuracy >90% on held-out query distribution
end-to-end latency within SLA including routing overhead
fallback rate monitored and alerted on surge

nodes.definition: Maintain versioned evaluation artifacts and track pass@k regressions across model and prompt updates, enabling rollback decisions and ablation of individual changes.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: benchmark revision or regression threshold recalibration needed

cons.claim: Versioned eval catches regressions before production; enables precise ablation of prompt/model changes
cons.example: pinned HumanEval snapshot catches 3pp regression from prompt refactor before deploy

failure_modes: Eval versioning overhead; stale pinned eval becomes misleading if benchmark updated
pinned 2022 HumanEval subset misses new problem types added later
acceptance_tests: unpinned eval suite drifting with benchmark updates
regression threshold too loose missing real degradation
rollback criteria undefined leading to subjective decisions
revisit_triggers: eval suite version pinned and tagged for each release
regression threshold defined (e.g., >2pp pass@1 drop triggers review)
rollback criteria documented before deployment

edges.why_related: HumanEval benchmark requires unbiased pass@k estimator
edges.benefit_of_coupling: correct estimator prevents overestimation of HumanEval scores
edges.risk_of_conflict: biased estimator silently inflates benchmark numbers
edges.example: unbiased Chen et al. estimator with n=200 for pass@100

edges.why_related: Public benchmark baseline triggers contamination audit
edges.benefit_of_coupling: goodhart mitigation anchors to same benchmark metric
edges.risk_of_conflict: without mitigation benchmark score misleads capability claims
edges.example: contamination scan after HumanEval baseline established

edges.why_related: Benchmark results require versioned snapshot for regression tracking
edges.benefit_of_coupling: versioned eval enables ablation of model and prompt changes
edges.risk_of_conflict: unversioned eval cannot isolate regression source
edges.example: HumanEval snapshot pinned at v1.0 for regression baseline

edges.why_related: pass@k metric motivates deeper correctness evaluation beyond unit tests
edges.benefit_of_coupling: functional correctness stress-tests what pass@k cannot catch
edges.risk_of_conflict: pass@k alone misses oracle gap (wrong logic that passes tests)
edges.example: mutation testing added after pass@k plateau detected

edges.why_related: Base model selection gates fine-tuning: architecture and license must be compatible
edges.benefit_of_coupling: selecting right base reduces fine-tuning data requirements
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong base model selection wastes full fine-tuning run
edges.example: StarCoder2-15B selected before domain SFT initiated

edges.why_related: Model selection provides both specialist and generalist for tradeoff comparison
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tradeoff analysis requires fixed base model as reference
edges.risk_of_conflict: analysis is invalid if base model changes during comparison
edges.example: DeepSeek-Coder-7B vs GPT-4 comparison on fixed task set

edges.why_related: Model selection determines parameter count and architecture affecting latency
edges.benefit_of_coupling: latency profiling grounds serving configuration
edges.risk_of_conflict: model switch requires full latency re-profile
edges.example: latency profiling run on selected DeepSeek-Coder-33B before commit

edges.why_related: Model selection determines which specialists are available to orchestration
edges.benefit_of_coupling: orchestration routing depends on specialist API endpoints
edges.risk_of_conflict: routing logic breaks if model APIs change post-selection
edges.example: orchestration config lists specialist model IDs from selection

edges.why_related: Sandbox is a hard prerequisite for safe code execution in repair loop
edges.benefit_of_coupling: sandbox provides pass/fail signal that drives repair iterations
edges.risk_of_conflict: unsandboxed execution is a critical security risk
edges.example: TDG loop enabled only after sandbox security review passes

edges.why_related: RL from execution feedback requires safe execution to compute reward
edges.benefit_of_coupling: sandbox enables large-scale reward signal collection
edges.risk_of_conflict: unsandboxed RL training is a critical security risk
edges.example: RLEF training runs exclusively inside hardened sandbox

edges.why_related: Execution filtering of synthetic data requires sandbox to run generated solutions
edges.benefit_of_coupling: sandbox ensures filter correctness by actual execution
edges.risk_of_conflict: without sandbox, synthetic data quality filters are unreliable
edges.example: AlphaCode-style synthesis pipeline uses execution sandbox for filtering

edges.why_related: Sandbox execution surfaces security-relevant behaviors that SAST misses
edges.benefit_of_coupling: combining sandbox execution with SAST provides defense in depth
edges.risk_of_conflict: sandbox alone does not catch credential leakage in non-executing code paths
edges.example: SAST runs on code before sandbox execution as complementary layer

edges.why_related: Sandbox execution is required for mutation testing and fuzz testing
edges.benefit_of_coupling: functional correctness eval requires safe execution environment
edges.risk_of_conflict: without sandbox functional correctness is limited to static analysis
edges.example: mutation testing runs inside sandbox for each mutant execution

edges.why_related: TDG repair loop generates multiple candidates naturally enabling best-of-n selection
edges.benefit_of_coupling: combining repair loop with diversity sampling maximizes solution quality
edges.risk_of_conflict: running both without coordination wastes budget
edges.example: final solution selected from diverse repair traces after max iterations

edges.why_related: TDG loop outcomes provide training signal for RL reward function design
edges.benefit_of_coupling: execution traces from TDG loop improve RL reward shaping
edges.risk_of_conflict: reward hacking patterns discovered in TDG loop must be mitigated in RLEF
edges.example: repair loop failure traces used to shape partial-credit reward in RLEF

edges.why_related: Repository context retrieval shares infrastructure with API doc retrieval
edges.benefit_of_coupling: combined retrieval provides both structural and signature grounding
edges.risk_of_conflict: without coordination, repo and API retrieval may exceed context window budget
edges.example: unified retrieval pipeline with token budget split between repo and API context

edges.why_related: Component library imports from repo context enable front-end generation grounding
edges.benefit_of_coupling: repo context provides actual component usage patterns from codebase
edges.risk_of_conflict: without repo context, front-end generation ignores existing component conventions
edges.example: existing React component usage patterns retrieved and injected for new component generation

edges.why_related: Existing data pipeline code from repo context informs Python data-science generation
edges.benefit_of_coupling: repo context prevents re-implementing existing utility functions
edges.risk_of_conflict: without repo context, model generates duplicate utilities
edges.example: existing pandas utility functions retrieved before generating new pipeline steps

edges.why_related: Web/HTML specialization is implemented through stack-specific prompt and few-shot design
edges.benefit_of_coupling: stack prompt provides the primary encoding of React/HTML idioms
edges.risk_of_conflict: stale stack prompt directly degrades web generation quality
edges.example: React 18 hooks prompt version 2.1 used for web generation task router

edges.why_related: Python data-science specialization is implemented through pandas/numpy-specific prompts
edges.benefit_of_coupling: stack prompt provides vectorization conventions and shape assertion patterns
edges.risk_of_conflict: stale stack prompt with old pandas idioms causes deprecation errors
edges.example: pandas 2.0 compatible prompt version 3.0 used for data-science task router

edges.why_related: Component library API signatures ground front-end generation in valid props
edges.benefit_of_coupling: accurate API injection prevents hallucinated props and invalid attributes
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong component library version causes prop type mismatches
edges.example: shadcn/ui v2 API signatures injected for React component generation

edges.why_related: pandas/numpy/sklearn API signatures ground data-science generation in valid method calls
edges.benefit_of_coupling: accurate API injection prevents deprecated method hallucination
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong library version causes silent runtime deprecation errors
edges.example: pandas 2.0 API signatures injected for data pipeline generation

edges.why_related: Fine-tuned specialist is one half of the specialist-vs-generalist comparison
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tradeoff analysis requires fine-tuned specialist as the comparison subject
edges.risk_of_conflict: cannot perform tradeoff analysis without a fine-tuned candidate
edges.example: 7B specialist fine-tuned on 10K internal examples compared to 70B generalist

edges.why_related: SFT checkpoint provides stable base policy required for RL training
edges.benefit_of_coupling: RL builds on SFT to further improve functional correctness
edges.risk_of_conflict: RL on unstable policy causes reward collapse; SFT must precede RL
edges.example: RLEF training initiated from SFT checkpoint at 95% convergence

edges.why_related: Fine-tuned specialists are the primary assets deployed in orchestration
edges.benefit_of_coupling: orchestration value depends on specialist quality
edges.risk_of_conflict: poor specialist quality makes orchestration routing counterproductive
edges.example: fine-tuned Python specialist deployed as ORCH_CODEGEN specialist endpoint

edges.why_related: Synthetic data augments training dataset for fine-tuning
edges.benefit_of_coupling: larger verified dataset improves fine-tuning sample efficiency
edges.risk_of_conflict: contaminated synthetic data degrades fine-tuned model quality
edges.example: 100K execution-filtered synthetic examples added to 10K human-labeled dataset

edges.why_related: Goodhart mitigation protocol defines what gets included in versioned eval suite
edges.benefit_of_coupling: versioned eval must include contamination-clean held-out problems
edges.risk_of_conflict: without goodhart check, versioned eval may include contaminated problems
edges.example: held-out internal suite included in versioned eval snapshot after contamination audit

edges.why_related: Specialist-vs-generalist decision determines orchestration specialist pool composition
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tradeoff analysis results directly inform routing strategy
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong tradeoff decision leads to cost-inefficient or quality-degraded routing
edges.example: tradeoff analysis recommends 7B specialist for Python tasks and 70B generalist for multi-modal tasks

edges.why_related: Latency profiles constrain orchestration routing decisions and SLA commitments
edges.benefit_of_coupling: latency data enables SLA-aware routing with fallback thresholds
edges.risk_of_conflict: routing without latency data causes SLA violations under load
edges.example: routing timeout set to p95 latency of specialist plus 20% headroom

edges.why_related: Docstring quality is a precondition for TDG loop to converge correctly
edges.benefit_of_coupling: complete specs prevent repair loop from converging to wrong interpretation
edges.risk_of_conflict: ambiguous specs cause repair loops to plateau on wrong function behavior
edges.example: docstring quality gate runs before TDG loop initiation

edges.why_related: Docstring quality constrains diversity sampling: ambiguous specs produce diverse but wrong candidates
edges.benefit_of_coupling: structured docstrings focus sampling diversity on correct solution space
edges.risk_of_conflict: ambiguous docstrings cause diverse sampling to explore wrong solution space
edges.example: docstring I/O examples anchor diversity sampling to correct output

edges.why_related: Diverse candidate pool enables stronger functional correctness evaluation via selection
edges.benefit_of_coupling: best-of-n selection from diverse candidates improves mutation kill rate
edges.risk_of_conflict: single greedy candidate limits functional correctness signal
edges.example: mutation testing applied to top-3 diverse candidates for correctness audit

edges.why_related: RLEF-trained model generates higher-quality diverse candidates for sampling
edges.benefit_of_coupling: diversity sampling benefits from RLEF-improved base policy quality
edges.risk_of_conflict: without RLEF improvement, diverse sampling over low-quality candidates wastes compute
edges.example: RLEF model used as generator in best-of-n diversity sampling pipeline

edges.why_related: Security scan is a mandatory gate before orchestration returns code to user
edges.benefit_of_coupling: orchestration must not bypass security gate under latency pressure
edges.risk_of_conflict: security gate bypass exposes users to SQL injection or credential leakage
edges.example: ORCH_CODEGEN pipeline enforces SAST gate before result returned

edges.why_related: Goodhart mitigation reveals that public benchmark score is insufficient capability signal
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension between reporting benchmark and requiring held-out eval
edges.risk_of_conflict: teams resist goodhart check as overhead to quick benchmark reporting
edges.example: always report held-out internal eval alongside public benchmark; never benchmark-only
edges.resolution_rule: Use contamination-filtered held-out eval alongside public benchmark; never report only public pass@k

edges.why_related: Tradeoff analysis may conclude fine-tuning is not worth the cost
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension between investing in fine-tuning vs using generalist with prompt engineering
edges.risk_of_conflict: teams over-invest in fine-tuning before completing tradeoff analysis
edges.example: complete cost-benefit analysis before committing GPU compute to fine-tuning
edges.resolution_rule: Run cost-benefit analysis before committing to fine-tuning; generalist may suffice with prompt engineering

edges.why_related: Latency SLA conflicts with maximizing repair iterations in TDG loop
edges.benefit_of_coupling: more repair iterations improve quality but increase per-query latency
edges.risk_of_conflict: teams increase iteration cap without verifying SLA impact
edges.example: cap repair iterations to fit latency SLA; measure end-to-end latency after cap change
edges.resolution_rule: Cap repair iterations to fit latency SLA; trade accuracy improvement for latency when budget exceeded

edges.why_related: Synthetic data generation risks contaminating evaluation benchmarks
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension between maximizing training data and eval benchmark integrity
edges.risk_of_conflict: synthetic data pipeline accidentally includes benchmark problem solutions
edges.example: deduplication against eval benchmarks required before any synthetic data added to training
edges.resolution_rule: Deduplicate synthetic data against eval benchmarks; run contamination scan after any synthesis run

conflict_axes.description: Optimizing benchmark pass@k causes contamination and reward hacking that decouples from real code quality
conflict_axes.mitigation: held-out internal eval alongside public benchmark

conflict_axes.description: Fine-tuned specialists outperform on narrow tasks but degrade outside distribution; generalists cover more tasks at higher cost per token
conflict_axes.mitigation: empirical cost-benefit analysis with held-out task distribution before committing to specialization

conflict_axes.description: More repair iterations improve functional correctness but compound token cost and latency; tight SLA forces early stopping
conflict_axes.mitigation: parameterized iteration cap with SLA-aware stopping criterion

conflict_axes.description: Strict sandbox isolation (gVisor, syscall filtering) adds per-execution overhead; looser isolation risks container escape
conflict_axes.mitigation: tiered sandbox: strict for untrusted inputs, lighter-weight for trusted eval fixtures

conflict_axes.description: Large synthetic datasets improve model coverage but risk contaminating evaluation benchmarks if overlap not controlled
conflict_axes.mitigation: mandatory deduplication and contamination scan before synthetic data added to training

conflict_axes.description: Injecting more repo/API context improves grounding but exceeds context window and introduces irrelevant noise
conflict_axes.mitigation: retrieval precision budget: cap tokens and measure retrieval precision on held-out tasks

conflict_axes.description: Execution-based RL reward can be hacked by models that generate exception-catching wrappers or test oracle leakage
conflict_axes.mitigation: mutation testing audit on RL-trained solutions to detect superficially-passing hacks

conflict_axes.description: Per-stack prompts improve accuracy but multiply maintenance surface; stale prompts actively mislead model generation
conflict_axes.mitigation: prompt versioning tied to framework release; automated staleness detection

conflict_axes.description: Aggressive SAST blocks insecure code but false positives create alert fatigue causing engineers to disable rules
conflict_axes.mitigation: precision-tuned rule sets with per-rule false-positive rate tracked; human review for ambiguous cases

conflict_axes.description: High-n diversity sampling for best-of-n raises pass@1 but multiplies inference cost linearly; budget forces n tradeoff
conflict_axes.mitigation: adaptive n based on verifier confidence; cache candidates across similar queries

edge_cases.description: HumanEval problem solutions present in model training data (contamination)
edge_cases.trigger: training corpus sourced from GitHub after HumanEval release (2021)
edge_cases.handling: run n-gram and semantic dedup against benchmark; report held-out internal scores

edge_cases.description: Container escape via unpatched kernel vulnerability in execution sandbox
edge_cases.trigger: CVE published for container runtime in use
edge_cases.handling: immediate sandbox update; fallback to stricter gVisor isolation; security alert

edge_cases.description: RL reward hacking: model generates try/except wrappers that catch all exceptions to pass tests
edge_cases.trigger: sudden pass@k improvement without corresponding mutation kill rate improvement
edge_cases.handling: mutation testing gate added to RL reward; exception-catching pattern blacklisted

edge_cases.description: Library version mismatch: API grounding uses wrong pandas/numpy version
edge_cases.trigger: library upgrade in production while grounding docs remain old
edge_cases.handling: version-pinned doc retrieval index; CI check verifying doc version matches runtime

edge_cases.description: Context window overflow from over-fetching repo context truncating critical instructions
edge_cases.trigger: large repo with many relevant files exceeds model context limit
edge_cases.handling: retrieval budget cap with priority ranking; truncation alerts

edge_cases.description: Catastrophic forgetting after domain fine-tuning: HumanEval baseline drops >5pp
edge_cases.trigger: SFT on narrow domain data without general coding data mixing
edge_cases.handling: data mixing with base general coding dataset; continuous HumanEval monitoring during training

edge_cases.description: Routing classifier distribution drift: production query types shift away from training distribution
edge_cases.trigger: product scope expansion or user behavior shift
edge_cases.handling: routing accuracy monitoring; retraining trigger when accuracy drops below threshold

edge_cases.description: Silent wrong answers: generated code passes tests but contains logical errors (oracle gap)
edge_cases.trigger: test suite too weak to distinguish correct from plausible-looking wrong code
edge_cases.handling: mutation testing and property-based testing to stress unit tests; expand test suite

edge_cases.description: Synthetic data mode collapse amplifying base model errors at scale
edge_cases.trigger: generation model used for synthesis has systematic blind spots
edge_cases.handling: diversity audit on synthetic data; include external seed problems from multiple sources

edge_cases.description: SAST false positives on safe parameterized queries blocking valid generated code
edge_cases.trigger: legacy SAST rule not updated for modern safe patterns
edge_cases.handling: rule precision audit quarterly; tiered alert (warn vs block) for contested rules

edge_cases.description: pass@k metric gaming via high temperature producing incoherent diverse outputs
edge_cases.trigger: temperature tuned to maximize pass@100 at expense of pass@1 quality
edge_cases.handling: report both pass@1 and pass@k>=10; track average solution quality independently

edge_cases.description: Stack-specific prompt staleness teaching deprecated framework patterns
edge_cases.trigger: framework major version release (React 19, pandas 2.0) while prompts not updated
edge_cases.handling: prompt version registry with framework version tags; automated staleness alerts on release

priority_rationale: Security-critical nodes (EXEC_SANDBOX, SECURITY_SCAN) first to prevent unsafe code execution. Model selection (CODELLM_SELECT) and capability baseline (CODEX_BENCH) gate all downstream work. Goodhart mitigation (GOODHART_BENCH) follows benchmark to prevent overestimation. Feedback loops (TDG_LOOP, CODEGEN_FINETUNE, RLEF) next as primary capability drivers. Context engineering (REPO_CONTEXT, API_GROUND, STACK_SPEC) and production concerns (INFER_LATENCY, ORCH_CODEGEN) follow. Stack specializations (WEB_HTML_GEN, PY_DATA_GEN), diversity, and doc quality are lower priority refinements.

dominance_rules.rule: When HumanEval pass@k is the only reported metric, REQUIRE contamination scan and held-out internal eval before any capability claim
dominance_rules.trigger_condition: public benchmark reported without contamination check
dominance_rules.rationale: post-2021 training data routinely includes HumanEval solutions

dominance_rules.rule: Execution sandbox MUST be in place before TDG_LOOP or RLEF are activated
dominance_rules.rationale: unsandboxed execution of generated code is a critical security risk

dominance_rules.rule: License review of base model MUST complete before fine-tuning or deployment investments are made
dominance_rules.rationale: license incompatibility discovered post fine-tuning wastes full training cost

dominance_rules.rule: Versioned eval snapshot MUST be pinned before any model or prompt change is shipped
dominance_rules.rationale: un-pinned eval cannot detect regressions from concurrent changes

dominance_rules.rule: Security scanning gate MUST run before generated code is returned to user or committed
dominance_rules.rationale: unscanned generated code may contain injection vulnerabilities or credentials

dominance_rules.rule: Specialist-vs-generalist cost-benefit analysis MUST precede fine-tuning commitment
dominance_rules.rationale: generalist with prompt engineering may match specialist at lower infra cost

dominance_rules.rule: Docstring spec completeness check SHOULD precede generation loop; incomplete specs warrant clarification before generation
dominance_rules.trigger_condition: generation on ambiguous or empty docstring
dominance_rules.rationale: ambiguous specs cause repair loops to converge on wrong interpretation

dominance_rules.rule: Unbiased pass@k estimator (n>=k samples) MUST be used; naive average over k attempts is prohibited
dominance_rules.trigger_condition: pass@k reported from single attempt per problem
dominance_rules.rationale: biased estimator over-reports capability by 5-15pp at common n/k ratios

dominance_rules.rule: Synthetic data deduplication against eval benchmarks MUST run before adding to training
dominance_rules.trigger_condition: synthetic data added to training without dedup check
dominance_rules.rationale: synthetic data contamination inflates eval benchmark scores

dominance_rules.rule: API grounding MUST use version-pinned docs matching production runtime; cross-version injection is prohibited
dominance_rules.trigger_condition: API docs version mismatches production library version
dominance_rules.rationale: wrong version docs cause silent runtime errors from deprecated APIs

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do NOT re-run fine-tuning after license discovery failure; complete CODELLM_SELECT (including license review) before starting CODEGEN_FINETUNE
anti_rework_rules.prevents: full GPU training run wasted on unlicensable model

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do NOT rebuild execution sandbox from scratch after security incident; harden iteratively with CVE patches rather than full rebuild
anti_rework_rules.prevents: repeated partial-rebuild cycles that miss root cause

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do NOT re-author stack-specific prompts from scratch on framework version upgrade; diff-update only changed idioms
anti_rework_rules.prevents: losing validated few-shot examples during bulk prompt rewrite

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do NOT run RLEF before CODEGEN_FINETUNE (SFT) baseline is stable; SFT stability is a prerequisite for RL policy stability
anti_rework_rules.prevents: RL training on unstable policy causing reward collapse requiring full restart

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do NOT add synthetic data to training after eval suites are pinned without re-running deduplication check
anti_rework_rules.prevents: benchmark contamination from synthetic data requiring eval suite re-pinning

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do NOT increase repair loop iteration cap without re-profiling end-to-end latency; SLA budget must be re-verified
anti_rework_rules.prevents: SLA breach discovered in production requiring emergency cap rollback

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do NOT change retrieval strategy (BM25 to dense) without re-validating context precision on held-out repo tasks
anti_rework_rules.prevents: silent context quality regression causing generation accuracy drop

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do NOT modify SAST rules without measuring false-positive impact on sampled generation outputs
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rule tightening blocking valid code causing user-facing regressions

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do NOT promote new model checkpoint to production without versioned eval regression report
Do NOT tune sampling temperature for pass@k without separately verifying pass@1 quality; report both metrics
anti_rework_rules.prevents: latent pass@1 degradation masked by pass@100 optimization

iteration_protocol.trigger: HumanEval pass@1 drops >2pp from previous release
iteration_protocol.action: run VERSIONED_EVAL regression report; ablate model and prompt changes; identify and revert regression source
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: regression source identified and addressed or decision documented

iteration_protocol.trigger: Container escape CVE published for sandbox runtime
iteration_protocol.action: immediate sandbox update; switch to stricter isolation mode; security review of affected generation logs
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: sandbox updated and penetration test passed

iteration_protocol.trigger: TDG_LOOP convergence failure: repair loop hits iteration cap without passing tests
iteration_protocol.action: inspect error trace; check if problem is unsolvable vs prompt/context issue; escalate to human review
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: problem flagged as unsolvable or prompt/context fixed with success

iteration_protocol.action: inspect routing confusion matrix; retrain or update classifier with new query examples
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: routing accuracy restored to >90% on held-out query set

iteration_protocol.trigger: SAST false-positive rate exceeds 15% on sampled outputs
iteration_protocol.action: audit rule set; tune or narrow rules; measure precision/recall tradeoff
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: false-positive rate <10% with no new true-positive regressions

iteration_protocol.trigger: Mutation kill rate on RL-trained solutions drops below 55%
iteration_protocol.action: audit for reward hacking patterns; add mutation-based penalty to reward function or filter
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: mutation kill rate >60% maintained across 500 sampled solutions

iteration_protocol.trigger: API grounding version mismatch detected (runtime vs doc version)
iteration_protocol.action: re-index API documentation corpus with pinned version; validate generation accuracy on version-sensitive tasks
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: doc version matches runtime; generation accuracy on version-sensitive tasks verified

iteration_protocol.trigger: Catastrophic forgetting: HumanEval drops >5pp after fine-tuning
iteration_protocol.action: revert to pre-fine-tuning checkpoint; adjust data mixing ratio to include more general coding data; retrain

iteration_protocol.trigger: Benchmark contamination scan returns positive signal
iteration_protocol.action: isolate contaminated problems from reporting; conduct held-out eval only; document and disclose limitation
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: clean held-out eval results reported with contamination disclosure
